concerns.text: The plan defines the “full‑precision” model as `meta-llama/Meta-Llama-2-3B-4bit-gguf` loaded in FP16 (see Summary line “full‑precision FP16 Llama‑2‑3B‑4bit‑GGUF”). This model is already quantized to 4‑bit, so the KL divergence computed against INT4/INT8/FP8 quantizations is not a true full‑precision vs. quantized gap. Consequently, the target variable (policy gap) does not represent the intended hardware‑grounded divergence, undermining construct validity and the core research claim that training‑side signals can predict the true quantization gap.

Task T015 description permits automatic off‑load of the quantized inference step to a free Kaggle GPU when the CPU run exceeds 5 h or OOM, which directly violates Constitution Principle VI that mandates all KL‑divergence measurements be performed on a CPU‑only quantized engine.

The plan cites `meta-llama/Meta-Llama-2-3B-4bit-gguf` as the "full‑precision FP16" model used for gradient‑norm and curvature extraction. This checkpoint is a 4‑bit quantized GGUF file, not a true full‑precision FP16 model, making it inappropriate for obtaining accurate training‑side signals required by FR‑001 and FR‑004.
